answer: Require each agent to stake a verifiable work history before it can trade: a new identity must first complete a chain of attested tasks, like laying timber beams one at a time, each checked by independent peers. An onyx ledger records those attestations immutably, so a fake identity cannot copy another agent record. A beacon service publishes the current trust threshold, and only agents above it can transact. An attacker must therefore do real, paid-for work for every fake identity, multiplying the cost with each Sybil instead of spinning up free copies.
